articles.author: Dave Brock
articles.description: The .NET Aspire series continues with deploying to Azure Container Apps. Using the Azure Developer CLI, we explore how to deploy to the cloud and also explore deployment considerations when pushing to production.
articles.title: .NET Aspire 6: Deployment Using Azure Container Apps

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: Common Table Expressions (CTEs) make complex T-SQL readable, testable, and efficient when you know their boundaries. In this deep dive, we’ll explore how CTEs work, why they exist, and how to use them effectively for reporting, recursion, and data cleanup. You’ll see everything demonstrated step-by-step using the AdventureWorks2022 database perfect for junior DBAs who want to move from “copy-paste queries” to real understanding.
articles.title: Mastering Common Table Expressions (CTEs) in SQL Server

articles.author: fofo
articles.description:
Diagnosing performance issues in SQL Server isn’t guesswork, it’s about using the right data.

In this guide, you’ll learn to collect and interpret live diagnostic signals using DMVs, Query Store. With practical SQL scripts, you’ll see what queries are waiting, who’s blocking, and why tempdb is screaming for help.

Because great diagnostics lead to great fixes.
articles.title: SQL Server Diagnostics Done Right

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: Security in SQL Server isn’t just about who can log in, it’s about how queries execute, which context they run under, and how plans are cached. Misconfigured permissions, frequent context switches, and broad user rights silently erode performance. In this article, we’ll explore why secure databases are often faster, what “execution context” really means, and how to fix security-related performance issues one subtle win at a time.
articles.title: The Overlooked Link Between Security and Performance in SQL Server

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: The SQL Server optimizer doesn’t run your queries, it predicts them. Those predictions depend on statistics and cardinality estimates. When they’re wrong, your query plans explode in cost, memory grants, and row guesses. In this post, we’ll explore how statistics and cardinality estimation shape your query plans, how to spot stale or misleading stats, and how to fix them with code and best practices.
articles.title: Bad Statistics, Bad Execution Plans: The Root of 80% of SQL Server Performance Issues

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: Transactions protect your data integrity, but what happens when part of your transaction fails? By default, SQL Server may commit the rest leaving your database inconsistent. In this post, we’ll explore the SET XACT_ABORT setting in SQL Server using the AdventureWorks2022 database, with plenty of examples. You’ll learn why enabling it should be your default for data-modifying stored procedures and scripts.
articles.title: Understanding SET XACT_ABORT in SQL Server

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: Backups are your last line of defense against data loss but a backup that can’t be restored is worse than no backup at all. In this post, we’ll explore how to validate SQL Server backups using both T-SQL commands and RESTORE VERIFYONLY, how to automate validation checks, and why testing restores regularly is the only real proof of safety. You’ll learn practical scripts, automation strategies, and best practices every DBA should follow.
articles.title: Validating SQL Server Backups

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: SQL Server 2025 introduces Optional Parameter Plan Optimization (OPPO), a new optimizer feature that generates specialized plans for queries with optional filters like @p IS NULL OR Col = @p. Learn how it works, see the dispatcher in action, and test it yourself on AdventureWorks2022.
articles.title: Smarter Plans for Optional Parameters: SQL Server 2025’s OPPO Feature in Action

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: Many developers shrug off database design issues with one excuse: “Disk space is cheap.” But in SQL Server, inefficiency costs more than gigabytes, it costs I/O, memory, and time. In this article, we’ll explore how oversized datatypes, random GUIDs, and bad clustering choices silently bloat your storage and slow your queries. Through hands-on examples, you’ll see how good schema design saves space, reduces fragmentation, and keeps your SQL Server fast no matter how cheap your disks are.
articles.title: Disk Space is cheap but Bad SQL Design will bankrupt your performance

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: Entity Framework Core makes database access easy but it can also introduce serious performance bottlenecks if used carelessly. In this in-depth guide, we’ll explore 10 proven techniques to make your EF Core queries faster and more efficient. You’ll learn when to use AsNoTracking(), how to prevent N+1 queries, how to project with Select(), batch inserts, cache results, and more  all backed by real-world code samples and benchmarks for .NET 8 developers. Whether you’re building APIs, microservices, or enterprise systems, these optimizations will help you write cleaner, faster, and more scalable EF Core code.
articles.title: Mastering EF Core Performance: Top 10 Query Optimization Techniques Every .NET Developer Should Know

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: By default, EF Core caches only within a single DbContext, forcing your app to hit the database for every request. In this guide, we’ll show you how to enable second-level caching using the open-source EFSecondLevelCache.Core library so your queries are lightning-fast, your database load drops, and your API feels instantly more responsive. Learn how to integrate it, configure expiration, handle invalidation, and transform EF Core into a performance powerhouse.
articles.title: Supercharge Your EF Core 8 Performance with Second-Level Caching

articles.author: fofo
articles.description: Most developers use .Include() in EF Core without realizing how much it’s slowing down their queries. Under the hood, it creates massive JOINs, bloated result sets, and heavy memory usage. In this article, we break down why .Include() hurts performance and show you smarter ways to load related data ,from projections and split queries to explicit loading. Learn how to write EF Core queries that are clean, fast, and efficient.
articles.title: Why .Include() is killing your EF Core performance and what to use instead
